sermon.title: The King’s Next Move
sermon.speaker: Guest speaker (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this message a guest speaker at Vine Cluster Church continues his study of Esther in chapters 8–10 as a parable of the new covenant. He teaches that the new covenant has authority over the old, that the ceremonial “shadow laws” point to Jesus while the moral law stays, and that Jesus gives his church power. He closes with the judgment on Jerusalem in AD 70 and a call to stand like Mordecai today.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The speaker is a guest, not Pastor Kincer, and continues the Esther study from “The King’s Servants” (“last week”); the recording does not give his name. Editor notes: he cites “Acts 2 4 46” (captioned), which is Acts 2:46, and “Acts 2 verse 43”; he reads Esther 9:5–16 and speaks of the 75,000 (Esther 9:16) in his own words; he says Timothy “wasn’t circumcised,” whereas Acts 16:3 says Paul had Timothy circumcised, so that remark is his own; he gives “Numbers 23:20” for a command to bless (Numbers 23:19–20 is shown). One spot is marked [unclear]. His historical statements (the date and death toll of the siege of Jerusalem in AD 70, quotes from a first-century historian that he says he looked up online, and events under later emperors) are his own and are not verified here. He also speaks about politics, about people mocking Christians, and about the Jews and the Pharisees; these are his own views and interpretations. He names his wife in passing; that appears in the transcript only.

faqs.question: Why does he say smart people can miss what Scripture means?
faqs.answer: He says there are people who are “really smart” but “their spiritual understanding is not that great because God Jesus Christ has to reveal it to you.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: At that time Jesus answered and said, “I thank You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that You have hidden these things from the wise and prudent and have revealed them to babes.

faqs.question: What stages of Christian growth does he describe?
faqs.answer: He says “you are born as a Christian you are a new believer you are a baby” and then you grow into “the child stage and the adolescent stage this is a teenager and then the young adult and the maturity stage.”

faqs.question: What does he say the holy of holies was?
faqs.answer: He says it was “where the presence would come, the word of God was there and you could understand God’s word,” and that since Jesus died anyone with a desire can come in.

faqs.question: Does he say God wants us to burn ourselves out?
faqs.answer: No. He says “God’s not looking for you to kill yourself he’s looking for you to submit,” a “responsive heart” that says “I want to lean on you.”

faqs.question: What does he say our sacrifices are today?
faqs.answer: He says “Jesus Christ is our sacrifice,” and “thanksgiving and praise and prayer” are the sacrifices now, even “when we come in on sundays and we’re tired.”

faqs.question: What does he say about work and the Sabbath commandment?
faqs.answer: He says “Jesus from the beginning is instituted work, we’re supposed to work,” and that the New Testament says “if you don’t work you shouldn’t eat.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat.

faqs.question: How big does he say the Persian empire was?
faqs.answer: He says it ran “from India to Ethiopia,” with “127 provinces,” and that in their day “this is a big empire a big kingdom huge.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: So the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month of Sivan, on the twenty-third day; and it was written, according to all that Mordecai commanded, to the Jews, the satraps, the governors, and the princes of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, one hundred and twenty-seven provinces in all, to every province in its own script, to every people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.

faqs.question: Does he say the book of Esther is history or just a story?
faqs.answer: He says “this actually happened the Bible is truth” and “it’s not just a story it’s not made up this is history,” and that “God can take a historical event and use it as an illustration.”

faqs.question: What does he say “power over the enemy” means?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus has given believers “power over the kingdom of darkness,” and “spiritually the kingdom of darkness can’t touch you because Jesus Christ is more powerful.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

faqs.question: What does he say about love in the church?
faqs.answer: He says “we need to have a love for one another that supersedes all of the issues we may have,” and that “our love for the church our love for God’s kingdom should be above all of the issues that we have with people.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then fear came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles. Now all who believed were together, and had all things in common, and sold their possessions and goods, and divided them among all, as anyone had need. So continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they ate their food with gladness and simplicity of heart, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily those who were being saved.

faqs.question: How many does he say were killed in Esther 9?
faqs.answer: He says Haman’s ten sons were destroyed, and “all together there were 75,000 killed throughout the empire.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Thus the Jews defeated all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, with slaughter and destruction, and did what they pleased with those who hated them. And in Shushan the citadel the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men. Also Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha— the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews—they killed; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder. On that day the number of those who were killed in Shushan the citadel was brought to the king. And the king said to Queen Esther, “The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the citadel, and the ten sons of Haman. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces? Now what is your petition? It shall be granted to you. Or what is your further request? It shall be done.” Then Esther said, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Shushan to do again tomorrow according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.” So the king commanded this to be done; the decree was issued in Shushan, and they hanged Haman’s ten sons. And the Jews who were in Shushan gathered together again on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred men at Shushan; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder. The remainder of the Jews in the king’s provinces gathered together and protected their lives, had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of their enemies; but they did not lay a hand on the plunder.

faqs.question: What does he say the commander did after the siege of Jerusalem?
faqs.answer: He says the commander “refused honor for this event,” saying he “merely served as an instrument of God’s wrath,” and that it “wasn’t an easy thing” for him to destroy the city.
